candidates.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents
candidates.summary: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. For small models, limited model capacity can result in lengthy reasoning that provides little useful guidance for action generation while incurring substantial inference cost. To address this challenge, we introduce Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR), a framework that reformulates reasoning as selection instead of open-ended generation. candidates.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
candidates.summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. candidates.title: How would you evaluate a personal AI for invented memories and revoked consent?
candidates.summary:
We are exploring YouBeyond, an early digital-self concept, before building a working system. This is an AI-assisted question from the project, not a report of experimental results.

How would you test a conversational model that represents a consenting person without rewarding it for simply sounding convincing?

A small evaluation could separate three failures: inventing a memory the person never supplied; turning an inference into a claimed fact about them; and continuing to use a fact after its permission is revoked. For example, after removing permission to use a workplace

candidates.title: Trloom: run TRL trainers (SFT, DPO, GRPO) from one YAML config
candidates.summary:
Hi all, I built Trloom, an open-source tool built on top of TRL. It reads one YAML file and builds the matching TRL trainer, so the training block maps to SFTConfig / DPOConfig / GRPOConfig.

Here is GRPO on Qwen2.5-0.5B with LoRA and accuracy_reward:

method: grpo model: model_name_or_path: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct dtype: bfloat16 use_peft: true lora_r: 16 lora_alpha: 32 dataset: path: HuggingFaceH4/Polaris-Dataset-53K train_split: train reward_funcs: - accuracy_reward training: output_dir: ./outputs/grpo-modal

candidates.title: SHAKTI — A Durga Puja cinematic built with WebGL and AI-assisted visuals 🪔
candidates.summary:
I wanted to experiment with combining real-time 3D scenes and generated cinematic footage into one continuous experience.

The result is SHAKTI, a 30-second interactive film that begins with a diya, assembles a golden Trishul, and ends with Maa Durga’s reveal.

Built with Three.js, WebGL, React, and a locally generated cinematic finale.

There’s also a separate interactive page exploring Durga Puja’s cultural traditions.
